cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: <important if="you are running lint or quality checks">
cards.claim: Task-specific rules in CLAUDE.md are wrapped in <important if="condition"> blocks so each loads into attention only when its condition matches, instead of sitting as flat always-on prose.
cards.evidence_detail: About 14 such blocks in a 278-line file (lint, db migrations, live db, logs, browser automation, tests/typechecks, rpi create-plan, test-it-locally, outline verification, rpi plugin edits, amend, devstack, ui copy, storybook, env files). No measurement in the file.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md: convert the long per-slice invariant sections (dispatcher, bill freeze, outbox) into conditional blocks keyed on the files being touched
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) Getting Claude to Actually Read Your CLAUDE.md (2026-03-17); repo itself at (A4)

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: so it prints just "✓ quality passed" on success and shows output ONLY on failure
cards.claim: The default lint/format check is a one-line command that wraps oxlint --quiet in a silent wrapper so a pass costs about one line of context and only a failure prints output.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated as design intent; the 'thousands of warnings' it avoids is asserted, not counted.
cards.landing: Phase routine / CI-equivalent local check: a single wrapped 'check' command the agent is told to use; backend ruff/mypy/lint-imports and web lint wrapped the same way

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Do NOT run `bun run lint` or `bun run format` directly unless you specifically need to read the warnings
cards.claim: CLAUDE.md names the noisy raw commands as forbidden and points to a quiet wrapper, so the guard is a named alternative, not just a prohibition.
cards.evidence_detail: Reason given: oxlint emits thousands of no-explicit-any warnings that flood the context window.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md 'Commands' section: pair each verbose command with its quiet equivalent

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: you must NEVER pipe the output of test commands to head/tail/grep/etc - you always want the full output
cards.claim: Never filter test output through head/tail/grep; rely on the Bash tool spooling long output to a persisted file and grep that file, so a long test run is never re-run just to see different lines.
cards.evidence_detail: Rationale: the spool message gives a path, so filtering the file is fast and avoids re-running slow commands.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md or a skill for test running; phase routine step for verification output

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Do not pipe test, typecheck, or quality output to head/tail/grep/etc.
cards.claim: A PreToolUse-style hook parses the Bash command, detects test/typecheck/lint invocations piped into head/tail/grep/sed/awk/less, and exits 2 with an explanatory message, enforcing the CLAUDE.md rule mechanically.
cards.evidence_detail: Regex matches bun/npm/yarn/pnpm test, test:ci, typecheck; turbo run test/typecheck; oxlint/oxfmt. Exit 2 blocks the call and feeds stderr to the model. The settings.json in the bundle has no hooks block, so wiring is not visible here.
cards.landing: Hooks (a harness review skipped hooks; this is a concrete small case: block a named bad command pattern, not a compliance audit)

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: OUTPUT=$(bun --bun run hook:quality 2>&1 && bun --bun turbo run typecheck 2>&1)
cards.claim: A Stop hook runs the quality and typecheck commands and exits 2 with the captured output on failure, so the agent cannot end its turn with a failing gate and is handed the errors to fix.
cards.evidence_detail: Output is captured into a variable and only echoed to stderr when exit code is nonzero; also runs a 'prebuild' step first. Success prints nothing.
cards.landing: Stop hook that runs the repo's check commands (hooks were skipped by the harness review; this is the backpressure-as-hook variant)

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Typecheck and quality checks are failing due to an ongoing merge.
cards.claim: The Stop hook has an escape hatch: during an unresolved merge (.git/MERGE_HEAD present) it skips the checks and tells the agent to keep working the conflict with the user, so the gate cannot trap the agent in a loop it cannot satisfy.
cards.evidence_detail: Still exits 2 with a message, i.e. it blocks stopping but redirects the work.
cards.landing: Any future Stop hook: list known states where the gate must not fire

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Usage: bun run scripts/run-silent.ts <description> <command> [args...]
cards.claim: The silent runner takes a description and a command, captures stdout and stderr, prints one green check line on success, and on failure prints a red cross, the failed command and the full combined output, then propagates the exit code.
cards.evidence_detail: About 48 lines of Bun/TypeScript; no output trimming on failure (the whole log is printed).
cards.landing: A small wrapper script in FixFlow's scripts/ used by the documented check commands (pytest, ruff, mypy, lint-imports, npm test, jest)

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: const VERBOSE = process.env.VERBOSE === "1";
cards.claim: The silent runner has a VERBOSE=1 environment switch that streams the raw command output, so the quiet default can be overridden when a human or agent needs everything.
cards.evidence_detail: Same switch exists in run_silent.sh and prints '→ Running: <command>' first.
cards.landing: Wrapper design: quiet by default, one documented opt-out

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: # Run test command and extract test count
cards.claim: The older bash wrapper (from the Makefile era, Go/Python/Jest) extracts a test count from pytest, jest, go or vitest output and prints it in the success line, so a pass still reports a number the agent can sanity-check.
cards.evidence_detail: run_silent_with_test_count greps '[0-9]+ passed' for pytest, numTotalTests via jq for jest, counts Action:pass for go, 'Test Files passed' for vitest.
cards.landing: Wrapper: print the pass count so 'zero tests ran' is visible (a quiet pass hides an empty test run)

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: # Run command with native quiet flags (output shown on failure)
cards.claim: Two wrapper modes exist: capture-everything-and-show-on-failure, and use-the-tool's-native-quiet-flag with failure output shown, plus section header helpers for multi-step make targets.
cards.evidence_detail: run_silent, run_with_quiet, print_header, print_main_header; a comment notes a removed tracking feature 'doesn't work across sub-makes'.
cards.landing: Backpressure scripts for the multi-tool check (backend + web + mobile)

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Erasing AGENTS.md and replacing with a symlink to CLAUDE.md
cards.claim: AGENTS.md is made a symlink to CLAUDE.md by 'make setup', so one instruction file serves Claude Code and other agents (Codex, OpenCode, Pi).
cards.evidence_detail: Implemented as rimraf AGENTS.md then ln -s CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md in the setup target.
cards.landing: Repo root: single source of agent instructions; relevant if FixFlow's agents ever include non-Claude tools

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.claim: A single 'check' target (typecheck then quality) is the one named entry point for a pre-handoff gate, identical to the root 'bun run check' script.
cards.evidence_detail: Both typecheck and quality are silent-wrapped; test is separate (bun run test).
cards.landing: One documented gate command per runtime that the phase routine and any Stop hook both call

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: This rule overrides direct test commands in plans, outlines, and tickets.
cards.claim: CLAUDE.md states an explicit precedence rule: the rule about running container-backed tests only via the root script wins over any test command written inside a plan, outline or ticket.
cards.evidence_detail: Context: packages needing test containers must never have their test scripts run directly; use 'bun run test:local:services', which starts services, waits, runs, cleans up.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md or phase routine: say which document wins when a plan's commands conflict with repo rules

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Never run their package test scripts directly.
cards.claim: Where a test needs infrastructure, the package script is declared off-limits and one root script owns setup, readiness wait, run and cleanup, so the agent cannot run the tests in a half-configured state.
cards.evidence_detail: Applies to riptide-api, billing, test-fixtures, electric-proxy and stale-daemon-sweeper.
cards.landing: Integration tests that need FIXFLOW_TEST_DATABASE_URL: wrap start/check/run/cleanup in one script

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: to add values to .env, don't read it, use echo "KEY=VALUE" >> .env
cards.claim: Agents are told to append to .env without reading it, keeping secrets out of context, and to consider .env.example for other developers.
cards.evidence_detail: Short rule inside an <important if> block about env variables.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md conditional block on env handling

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: The `Grep` and `Glob` and `Search` tools WILL NOT WORK. They do not traverse symlinks.
cards.claim: The task-notes directory is a symlink, so CLAUDE.md warns that search tools silently return nothing and requires Bash ls for exploration there.
cards.evidence_detail: A tool-limitation workaround recorded as a rule; the grind-design-discussion skill repeats it.
cards.landing: Any evidence/knowledge directory reached by symlink; also a general rule that a tool returning nothing is not proof of absence

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Assume the user already has the dev servers running — do not try to start them yourself
cards.claim: Agents are told which ports are the dev servers and to assume they are running rather than starting them, avoiding duplicate or colliding processes.
cards.evidence_detail: Ports 3000 and 5174 named.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md conditional block

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: do not use git commit --amend unless the user expressly requested it, just make a new commit
cards.claim: A conditional rule (when fixing a previous commit or doing a follow-on) forbids amend and requires a new commit.
cards.evidence_detail: One-line conditional block.
cards.landing: Phase routine commit rules (head SHA named by reviewer is stable only if history is not rewritten)

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Never stop another worktree's stack, its tmux session, or the shared Caddy to free a port
cards.claim: Parallel worktree stacks each have their own containers and ports but share one proxy, so agents are forbidden to stop another worktree's stack because another agent may be using it.
cards.evidence_detail: Part of the devstack block; each worktree runs its own stack in parallel.
cards.landing: Parallel-agent safety rule if multiple phases/worktrees run at once

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: use the linear branch name if known, otherwise use ENG-XXXX-twomore-words
cards.claim: Worktrees are created by a script with a fixed branch-naming convention tied to the ticket id, so every unit of work gets an isolated checkout with a predictable name.
cards.evidence_detail: scripts/create_worktree.sh; fallback is three short words when there is no ticket.
cards.landing: Phase routine: worktree/branch naming convention tied to the phase id

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: you MUST use the `/storybook` skill.
cards.claim: CLAUDE.md does not carry the detailed rules for a task domain; it carries a conditional pointer that names the skill the agent must load before touching that kind of file.
cards.evidence_detail: Same pattern for ui-copy (before writing any user-visible string), test-it-locally, and the rpi create-plan skill.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md slimming: move per-domain rules into skills, leave one conditional pointer each
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) Getting Claude to Actually Read Your CLAUDE.md; Skill Issue

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Use the `ui-copy` skill (`.claude/skills/ui-copy/SKILL.md`) before writing the string.
cards.claim: The ui-copy pointer lists the trigger by enumerating concrete cases (button, toast, tooltip, aria-label, error message) and gives a one-paragraph 'short version' so the most important rules are inline even if the skill is not loaded.
cards.evidence_detail: Condition text is a long enumerated list; the short version carries sentence case, no 'please', error shape and 'error.message is never a toast title'.
cards.landing: Skill-trigger wording in CLAUDE.md pointers: enumerate triggering cases and keep a short inline summary

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Add verification steps in "automated verification" that reference "use the test-it-locally skill
cards.claim: When a plan or structure outline is being written, CLAUDE.md tells the agent to read a named skill and write verification steps that invoke it, so plans carry executable verification by reference.
cards.evidence_detail: Plan validation steps are also standardised: typecheck, quality, test in that order (rpi:create-plan block).
cards.landing: Plan template: verification steps reference a named skill or script rather than free text; fixed validation triple

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Do NOT manually create SQL files - drizzle-kit generates them
cards.claim: Migrations are generated by the tool and never hand-written, with an indexing convention (few multi-column indexes, tenant id leftmost, single-column only for FK actions) and named exemplar files.
cards.evidence_detail: Conditional block triggered by changes under packages/db/src/tables. Points to commits.ts and pull-requests.ts as exemplars.
cards.landing: Conditional block on backend/app/**/models.py and alembic (FixFlow's migration rules already prose-heavy in CLAUDE.md)

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: This repository is a monorepo created by the HumanLayer team. It uses TurboRepo with Bun.
cards.claim: The whole CLAUDE.md is about 278 lines and is mostly a repo map, commands and conditional blocks; it contains no architecture rationale or history.
cards.evidence_detail: 278 lines, roughly 2,000 words; about 14 conditional blocks; structure section is 3 workspaces with one line per package.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md length target for FixFlow (390 lines now): comparison point for the trim
cards.inventory_ref: (A4) CodeLayer repo; (A3) Writing a good CLAUDE.md

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: <important if="the user asks you to make changes to the rpi: skill documents">
cards.claim: Where the source of installed skills lives differs from where the agent sees them, so CLAUDE.md states that edits to the skills belong in the repo path, not the installed copy.
cards.evidence_detail: Installed under ~/.humanlayer/riptide/..., source in apps/riptide-rpi-claude-plugin.
cards.landing: If FixFlow skills/workflows are ever installed elsewhere, record the canonical source path

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: ("spec needed", "research needed", "research in progress", "research in review", "ready for plan"
cards.claim: Ticket status is a fixed ladder (spec, research, plan, dev, code review, each with in-progress and in-review states) updated through a CLI, so workflow phase is externally visible state.
cards.evidence_detail: Full list: spec needed, research needed/in progress/in review, ready for plan, plan in progress/in review, ready for dev, in dev, code review.
cards.landing: Phase routine: externally visible phase status as an observable trace of compliance

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: `linear fetch-images ENG-XXXX` (do this any time the ticket has images in the description )
cards.claim: Agents have a CLI to fetch ticket images, with a rule to use it whenever the ticket contains images, so ticket context is complete.
cards.evidence_detail: Listed with other Linear CLI verbs (get-issue, add-comment, add-link, update-status, branch name).
cards.landing: Phase intake: fetch all ticket attachments

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: "MAX_THINKING_TOKENS": 32000
cards.claim: The project settings fix the thinking budget at 32,000 tokens through env, a repo-wide effort setting checked into the repository.
cards.evidence_detail: No comparison or rationale in the file.
cards.landing: Effort routing: a checked-in default thinking budget alongside per-agent model/effort in agent files

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: "CLAUDE_BASH_MAINTAIN_PROJECT_WORKING_DIR": "1"
cards.claim: Bash's working directory is pinned to the project directory every call, removing the cd-drift failure mode in long sessions.
cards.evidence_detail: Setting only; no explanation in file.
cards.landing: Project settings env block

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: "Bash(./scripts/spec_metadata.sh)"
cards.claim: The checked-in permission allow list is minimal: only the three invocation forms of one metadata script, so the project does not pre-approve broad command classes.
cards.evidence_detail: Three entries for scripts/spec_metadata.sh (relative, bare, via bash). The two hook scripts are not registered in this file.
cards.landing: Settings: narrow allowlist; note hooks need registration in settings to run

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: All non-trivial operations should be delegated to sub-agents.
cards.claim: A skill makes the main session an orchestrator that delegates research, codebase understanding and output-heavy shell work (aws, gh, logs) to sub-agents to keep long-horizon coherence.
cards.evidence_detail: Names codebase-analyzer, codebase-locator, pattern-locator and Bash sub-agents; 27 lines.
cards.landing: Skill for orchestrator sessions; maps to FixFlow's Haiku locator plus verbose-command delegation
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) Long-Context Isn't the Answer (sub-agents keep context small); /hl:orchestrate release 0.182.0

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: do not delegate multiple tasks that are likely to have significant overlap to separate sub-agents
cards.claim: Parallel sub-agents get separate tasks, but overlapping tasks must not be split across agents.
cards.evidence_detail: One sentence.
cards.landing: Workflow scripts: partition fan-out by non-overlapping scope

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: do not assume or begin working on a ticket autoatically.
cards.claim: With no task given, the orchestrator skill must ask what to work on; with a task given, it proceeds under the orchestration approach.
cards.evidence_detail: Prevents a skill load from starting unrequested work.
cards.landing: Skill design: a skill load never triggers work by itself

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Walk down each branch of the design tree, resolving dependencies between decisions one-by-one.
cards.claim: A 5-line interview skill: one question at a time, each with a recommended answer, walking the decision tree in dependency order until shared understanding.
cards.evidence_detail: Triggered by the phrase 'grill me'.
cards.landing: Skill for the owner-facing planning step before a phase starts

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: If a question can be answered by exploring the codebase, explore the codebase instead.
cards.claim: The interviewing agent must answer from the repository first and ask the human only what the repository cannot answer.
cards.evidence_detail: Also: 'Asking multiple questions at once is bewildering.'
cards.landing: Owner-question protocol in the phase routine

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Use these terms exactly — don't substitute "component," "service," "API," or "boundary."
cards.claim: A skill fixes a shared glossary (module, interface, implementation, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, locality) so agents and humans use the same terms in every design discussion.
cards.evidence_detail: Each term has an 'avoid' list; 'Rejected framings' section records definitions deliberately not used (Ousterhout depth ratio, 'boundary').
cards.landing: Skill: shared vocabulary for slice design; FixFlow already has slice/seam language in CLAUDE.md

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Imagine deleting the module. If complexity vanishes, it was a pass-through.
cards.claim: The deletion test decides whether a module earns its place: if deleting it makes complexity reappear across many callers it was deep, if complexity vanishes it was a pass-through.
cards.evidence_detail: Listed with 'the interface is the test surface' and 'one adapter is a hypothetical seam, two is a real one'.
cards.landing: Code-review/refuter checklist for abstraction added by an agent (anti-slop)

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Old unit tests on shallow modules become waste once tests at the deepened module's interface exist
cards.claim: When refactoring to a deeper module, replace the old unit tests with tests at the new interface instead of layering new tests on top; tests should assert observable outcomes and survive internal refactors.
cards.evidence_detail: Also classifies dependencies into four categories (in-process, local-substitutable, remote-but-owned, true external) that decide the test approach.
cards.landing: Test policy for refactor phases

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Spawn 3+ sub-agents in parallel using the Agent tool. Each must produce a **radically different** interface
cards.claim: Design-it-twice: three or more parallel sub-agents each get a different constraint (minimise interface, maximise flexibility, optimise the common caller, ports and adapters) and the orchestrator compares and recommends, with an explicit hybrid option.
cards.evidence_detail: The human gets a problem-space explanation while sub-agents run, so wait time is used. Based on Ousterhout. Each sub-agent output has 5 required parts.
cards.landing: A saved workflow script for design decisions (judge panel already exists; this is the divergent-generation counterpart)

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: walk back a good stretch of the commit history (`git log --oneline`) to find the codebase's hot spots
cards.claim: Architecture review is scoped by recency: hot spots from git history get attention first, because deepening pays off where future changes will land (YAGNI).
cards.evidence_detail: A named direction from the user skips the inference; scattered history means widen the net.
cards.landing: Scoping rule for audits and cleanup phases in the ship plan

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Do NOT propose interfaces yet.
cards.claim: The review skill produces a self-contained HTML report with a before/after picture and a strength badge per candidate, then stops and asks which to explore, so choice stays with the human before any design is proposed.
cards.evidence_detail: HTML written to the OS temp dir so nothing lands in the repo; Tailwind and Mermaid via CDN; strengths: Strong, Worth exploring, Speculative.
cards.landing: Owner-view format: a visual one-page report with ranked candidates

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Want me to record this as an ADR so future architecture reviews don't re-suggest it?
cards.claim: When the human rejects a candidate for a load-bearing reason the agent offers an ADR so later reviews do not re-litigate it, and offers only when a future explorer would actually need it (not for ephemeral reasons).
cards.evidence_detail: Candidates that contradict an existing ADR are surfaced only if friction is real, marked with a warning callout. CONTEXT.md holds the domain glossary, updated inline as terms are sharpened.
cards.landing: Decision records / knowledge store: record rejected options with reason so refuters do not re-raise them

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: disable-model-invocation: true
cards.claim: Heavy, user-initiated skills carry disable-model-invocation in frontmatter so the model never auto-triggers them; other skills use 'user-invocable' or a trigger phrase in the description.
cards.evidence_detail: Also bump-version uses user-invocable: true; grill-me triggers on the phrase 'grill me'; calldiff declares requires_bin and command.
cards.landing: Skill frontmatter conventions for the FixFlow skills being added

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Diff call stacks across git commits for agentic code review (22 languages).
cards.claim: A call-graph tool diffs call stacks between two git trees (diff), finds all paths from an entrypoint to a target symbol (reach), and prints a call tree (tree), as review input.
cards.evidence_detail: Skill is a CLI reference (npm i -g calldiff); maxDepth default 12; output is shown in a fenced diff block for colouring. No evidence of effect on review quality.
cards.landing: Call-graph tooling (harness review skipped it): reach from a router to a repository write, diff of call stacks in a PR for the Opus reviewer

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: **DO NOT read ticket files** - research must stay objective about the current codebase.
cards.claim: Research documents are kept objective by withholding the ticket from the researcher; the research phase only documents what exists, without critique, root cause or recommendations.
cards.evidence_detail: Fits the RPI/QRSPI split where questions are generated first; here the rule bans ticket reads and bans 'suggest improvements' unless asked.
cards.landing: Cold-resume trial design and research step: blind the reader to the conclusion/ticket
cards.inventory_ref: (B) March 2026 - Everything We Got Wrong About Research-Plan-Implement (research prompts returning opinions)

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Spawn sub-agents to verify each claim is still accurate
cards.claim: An autonomous second pass on a finished document: find thin sections, fill gaps with locator/analyzer/pattern/web sub-agents, then re-read and verify each factual claim (paths, lines, function names) with sub-agents before updating the doc.
cards.evidence_detail: Steps: read fully, gap analysis, spawn, claim verification, update, split if over 1000 lines, summarise using a template.
cards.landing: Saved workflow: claim-verification pass over any diagnosis/knowledge-store entry

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Check if any document is over 1000 lines
cards.claim: A document over 1000 lines is split into 2 to 3 by subject boundary without asking the user.
cards.evidence_detail: Also: read mentioned files FULLY without limit/offset before spawning; never write the document with placeholder values; wait for all sub-agents before synthesis.
cards.landing: Size ceiling for evidence/knowledge docs

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Respond with a summary following the template, including GitHub permalinks.
cards.claim: Final answers follow a template file referenced from the skill ({SKILLBASE}/references/...) and cite GitHub permalinks, so output shape and citations are fixed.
cards.evidence_detail: The template files are not in the bundle. Document writes in the task directory return a cloud permalink via a hook's additionalContext.
cards.landing: Six-question closing message as a template file inside a skill; permalinks (commit SHA links) in every claim

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: **Do NOT answer any of the existing design questions**
cards.claim: The autonomous review pass may add assumptions, options and new questions but must not answer open questions, change resolved ones, or add scope, keeping decisions with the human.
cards.evidence_detail: Plus: no new features or requirements; only deepen understanding of what is already scoped.
cards.landing: Reviewer/refuter scope limit in the phase routine: surface, do not decide

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: When documents conflict, the most recent document wins: design discussion > research > ticket
cards.claim: Document precedence is explicit: the design discussion beats research beats the ticket, because it captures decisions made after reading the other two.
cards.evidence_detail: Same skill: if several patterns exist, move it from 'patterns to follow' into a design question.
cards.landing: Precedence rule between ship plan, phase plan, decisions journal and CLAUDE.md

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: If you find multiple patterns to accomplish a task, remove it from "patterns to follow"
cards.claim: When the codebase shows two or more ways to do the same thing, the pattern is withdrawn from the 'patterns to follow' list and turned into an explicit design question rather than picking one silently.
cards.evidence_detail: Part of the pattern-verification step of the grind pass.
cards.landing: Plan review checklist: conflicting precedents become questions

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: You _MUST_ stop and ask the user how they would like to proceed after presenting the analysis
cards.claim: Conflict resolution is a human-gated procedure: sub-agents analyse both sides, the agent presents HEAD vs incoming vs a recommendation per conflict group, and changes happen only after the user confirms each one, tracked on a todo list.
cards.evidence_detail: Reads the ticket and structure outline first for task context; commit message records what each conflict was and how it was resolved.
cards.landing: Skill for merging main into phase branches (FixFlow phases run one per session so conflicts are likely)

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Commit first (derivation errors on uncommitted edits), verify while the bump commit is HEAD
cards.claim: A release skill lists every file that must carry the same version, then verifies by running the version-derivation scripts against the bump commit, where any other output means files are out of sync.
cards.evidence_detail: Versions are bases; releases derive base plus commits since the base changed. Never hand-pick a patch. The verification is a derived output equal to the new base.
cards.landing: Verification by executable derivation, not by agent assertion; FixFlow Alembic head and CLAUDE.md head number are the same shape of drift

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: If a sentence only restates the point you just made, it's a summary tap.
cards.claim: A skill for fixing AI-sounding prose records Dex's edits: delete summary-tap sentences, distrust symmetry, replace category labels with remembered details, own the claim, use the field's exact word, and keep lines that do no argumentative work.
cards.evidence_detail: Written by Claude from rounds of editing with Dex on the software-factories essay; includes worked before/after examples. Says AI tell is tidiness, not bad grammar.
cards.landing: Writing skill for owner-facing one-page view and closing messages (reduce tidy filler)

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: make the file follow its own rules.
cards.claim: Dex's feedback on the writing skill itself was to make the file obey its own rules, i.e. instruction files should be audited against their own guidance.
cards.evidence_detail: A dated note (2026-07-17) at the top says the previous pass left a summary tap in the section defining summary taps.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md trim: audit the file against the length and clarity rules it asks agents to follow

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Pick one verb for one action and reuse it every time
cards.claim: Controlled-English rewriting (one word one meaning, active voice, simple tense, one instruction per sentence, at most 20 words per instruction, at most 3-word noun stacks) is applied to text another agent must parse: error messages, tool descriptions, inter-agent instructions.
cards.evidence_detail: Rewrite yields a rule/original/simplified table; refuses to drop safety conditions or qualifiers; cites ASD-STE100 Issue 9 (53 rules, ~900 approved words).
cards.landing: Style rules for CLAUDE.md invariants and subagent prompts: consistent verbs, short instructions

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Mechanical findings batch; voice findings go one at a time
cards.claim: When changing existing text the skill separates mechanical findings (one right answer, fix in batch) from voice findings (a prompt to look, a human decides one at a time); an audit that proposes 180 rewrites has stopped reading and started matching.
cards.evidence_detail: Also: change the defect not the sentence; if the rewrite is only more conformant, stop; when unsure which kind, treat it as voice.
cards.landing: Refuter/lint-fix policy: batch only findings with one right answer; escalate judgement calls singly

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: write to the person, never about the system.
cards.claim: The first rule of the copy skill is to describe what a state means for the user and what to do next, never the internal state; it supplies before/after pairs and a glossary table (use vs not) to keep one name per concept.
cards.evidence_detail: Includes error shape 'Could not <verb> <object>' plus what is true now and what to do; status label map; 'never render a raw enum'; ~14.5 KB file with shape and glossary tables.
cards.landing: Mobile app copy for technicians once skills exist; glossary-table pattern for one-name-per-concept

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Test the changed behavior and its stored state, not just whether the app loads.
cards.claim: The local verification skill requires checking both the UI result and the database end state of the changed flow, with the stack's health read from one status command before anything starts.
cards.evidence_detail: Steps: devstack status (read the whole output incl. an API healthcheck line), sync only if stale, headless browser, exercise the flow, verify rows with psql.
cards.landing: Fail-before/pass-after evidence: assert DB end state through a named local command in the phase's verification step

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Both are needed so multiple devstacks can run browser checks in parallel without sharing state.
cards.claim: Parallel agents are isolated by keying the browser session and profile to the per-worktree stack id, with explicit prohibitions on fixed profile names and fixed ports.
cards.evidence_detail: Rule: set AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION and AGENT_BROWSER_PROFILE from status at the start of every shell call; never run an unscoped 'agent-browser close'.
cards.landing: Parallel verifier isolation in workflow scripts

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Never put a credential value in a command, response, screenshot, log, or committed file.
cards.claim: Test credentials are loaded by sourcing the root .env and referenced by variable name, never extracted by grep, and the agent must not take screenshots after entering credentials or ask the user to paste them in chat.
cards.evidence_detail: Explains that grep/cut leaves wrapping quotes in the value; if variables are missing the user adds them to .env.
cards.landing: Credential-handling block for the Expo/web test flows

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Read more if needed: [references/devstack.md](references/devstack.md).
cards.claim: Skills use progressive disclosure: the main file carries the workflow and links to reference files (devstack, local CLI testing, agent-browser) that are read only when needed.
cards.evidence_detail: codebase-design does the same with DEEPENING.md and DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md under a 'Going deeper' heading.
cards.landing: Skill structure for FixFlow: short SKILL.md plus on-demand references

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: it is ok to request against the durable streams server directly.
cards.claim: For local testing the skill allows bypassing the production auth proxy to hit an internal service directly, while stating that production code is forced through the proxy.
cards.evidence_detail: Requires understanding how the proxy maps routes to the stream URL.
cards.landing: Test seams that bypass auth only locally

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Each mockup must be a single self-contained file
cards.claim: UI mockups are a single self-contained HTML file with inline CSS and JS in the task directory, because the viewer serves each artifact from its own signed URL and sibling files render unstyled; annotations and multiple states are required.
cards.evidence_detail: Includes a full design-token system (colours, 0 radius, mono type) and the rule 'keep it rough'.
cards.landing: Owner-view and mockup artefacts as single-file HTML

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: just outline the tree in each case
cards.claim: A 9-line skill makes the agent show a component tree as an indented outline annotated with state and which package each node comes from, instead of prose.
cards.evidence_detail: Precursor of the /show-me skill (visual representations instead of prose).
cards.landing: Compact structural views in review output (tree of slice calls instead of prose)
cards.inventory_ref: (A3) show-me: a coding agent skill for compact visual representations (2026-08-12)

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: purely cosmetic, zero behaviour change.
cards.claim: Every lint-rule suppression in the React linter config has a written reason, per rule or per file, and style-nit rules are turned off while Security, Bugs and Maintainability are errors and Performance is off.
cards.evidence_detail: Categories: Security error, Bugs error, Maintainability error, Accessibility warn, Performance off. Per-file overrides explain why a rule does not apply (e.g. 280 instances of a cosmetic rule).
cards.landing: Lint/refuter policy: only correctness categories gate; every suppression carries a reason so a reviewer can refute it

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: 'deslop/unused-export'
cards.claim: The linter includes a 'deslop' rule set (unused-export is the one named) as part of the automated slop defence, with exceptions documented where an export is deliberate API surface.
cards.evidence_detail: Exception is for src/collections: create...Collection factories exported for ReturnType derivation.
cards.landing: Dead-code checks (vulture/ts-prune equivalents) as backpressure against agent-added unused code

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Run `./scripts/setup-agent-browser.sh` to generate an encryption key for agent-browser session storage.
cards.claim: Human-only setup steps live in a separate HUMANS.md, kept out of CLAUDE.md, with an encrypted persistent browser session so agents reuse authenticated sessions without re-logging in.
cards.evidence_detail: 12 lines; README says a build from source sends nothing to HumanLayer and telemetry stays off when env is unset.
cards.landing: Move human-only onboarding out of CLAUDE.md into a separate file

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Library documentation research
cards.claim: For up-to-date library docs the agent is routed to a dedicated library-researcher tool (and also when the user says 'use context7'), instead of recalling API from memory.
cards.evidence_detail: Tool name mcp__humanlayer__library_researcher.
cards.landing: A docs-lookup agent/skill for Expo SDK 52 and SQLAlchemy 2.0 specifics

cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: if updating a packages to latest - run `bun pm view PACKAGE_NAME` to see the latest version
cards.claim: Dependency upgrades are done by looking up the latest version with the package manager and pinning it explicitly, instead of letting the agent guess a version.
cards.evidence_detail: Followed by 'bun add PACKAGE@VERSION'; also dependencies are installed only in the package that needs them.
cards.landing: Dependency-change rule

Cards R01-5 and R01-6 describe the scripts only.

Files referenced by the skills but not in the bundle were not read: improve-codebase-architecture/HTML-REPORT.md, test-it-locally/references/*, asd-ste100/references and examples, grind-research references/research_final_answer.md, grind-design-discussion references/design_discussion_final_answer.md.

Skills present in the repo but not in my file list (agent-browser, better-github-skill, chrome-devtools-cli, effect-program-design, html-demo-video-guidelines, migrate-orpc-to-effect, narrow-react-prop-types, no-use-effect, react-doctor, rebase-drizzle-migration, storybook, stripe-billing-verification) were not read.
The scripts hack/run_silent.sh and bun run quality / hook:quality definitions (package.json) were not in the bundle, so the exact oxlint --quiet wiring and what 'hook:quality' runs are unverified.

All repo files are undated in the bundle; source_date is the repo open-source date from the inventory (2026-10-22) and is an estimate. Authorship of individual files is unknown (author set to Dex+others); improve-writing explicitly records Dex's edits.
The repo files are the only evidence; no measurement of the effect of the <important if> blocks or the hooks is given in them.
